 Good morning! Here's the latest in trending: 

 Press badges: Judge lifts White House ban on CNN ( WBD ), MS NOW ( VSNT ), Politico.

 The Claude: Gene-editing stocks fall after Anthropic's  CRISPR-like discovery .

 Hardware push: Meta ( META )  unveils keychain-sized Charm gadget for Muse AI agent.


 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Top News
 
 
 
 G2 showdown 
 
 
 
Getty Images 
 
 
 The last time President Xi Jinping of China came to the United States on a state visit was during the Obama administration. So his arrival this week is a big deal. Xi touched down Wednesday evening at Andrews Air Force Base outside of Washington, D.C., where President Trump greeted him on the tarmac for the beginning of his three-day tour, which includes a dinner tonight featuring the CEOs of Alphabet ( GOOGL ), Apple ( AAPL ), Citigroup ( C ), Dell ( DELL ), Nvidia ( NVDA ), and Tesla ( TSLA ).

 'Partners, not rivals': Those were the first words Xi used to describe his vision for the U.S. and China, adding that "both [are] great countries, and their peoples are great as well." The easing of bilateral relations is definitely a major focus of the trip, with both sides agreeing to extend a trade truce just before the summit. That will build on the thaw in tensions that followed a tariff war with levies that extended beyond 100%, and subsequently led to the resumption of critical rare earths from Beijing .

Trade is likely to make the biggest headlines, such as announcements on agricultural purchases and non-tariff barriers, or the possibility of more high-end computer chips to China (maybe a reference to the AI arms race as well?) Other topics to be covered include geopolitics, with severe conflicts still raging across the globe. Discussions will take place on the economic support China gives Iran and Russia, as well as the multi-billion-dollar arms deals between the U.S. and Taiwan.

 Cars and planes: Perhaps the biggest sector on the American side to watch from a commercial standpoint is the mobility industry. Boeing ( BA ) has effectively been shut out of China since 2017 as its rival Airbus ( EADSY ) continued to expand its market share in the country, so stay tuned to see whether a deal is possible . Last week, President Trump also announced he's not opposed to Chinese automakers manufacturing cars in the U.S. as long as they employ Americans, which would allow them to bypass tariffs and potentially upend the domestic auto landscape.
